newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - CPFL common cut to hold.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - CPFL common cut to hold.

text.p: -- Investment bank Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said it has downgraded its recommendation on common shares of Brazilian state-owned power firm Companhia Paulista de Forca e Luz (CPFL) to hold from buy.
-- The bank said it is maintaining its buy recommendation on preferred shares of CPFL, which is owned by Sao Paulo state.
-- The bank said CPFL common, or ON shares, rose 145 percent in fiscal year 1996 and are up 11 percent so far this year as a result of optimism regarding the company's prospects for privatization.

-- Assuming the firm were sold off in 1997 and benefits from the privatization were seen in 1998, CPFL common would be worth $141 per 1,000 shares compared with its current price of aout $127.38, it added.

-- "At this level, the company's 1997 sales would be $165 per megawatt hour, in line with the amount paid for Cerj's privatization, the highest privatization price achieved up to now in Brazil," the bank said.
-- As a result, the upside potential would be limited to eight percent, it said.

-- It added it has maintained its buy rating on the cheaper CPFL preferred, which now trades at 19-percent discount to the common and would have a 33-percent upside potential in light of privatization.
-- CPFL common was up 0.40 reais at 133 reais while the preferred was untraded at its Wednesday closing price of 109 reais at 1350 local/1550 GMT on the Sao Paulo bourse.
